Two-way solute\,$\times$\,solvent cluster bootstrap, $5$th and $95$th percentiles. Row-identical strata are one row set: drawn once and printed once, under the row set's first name above and restated under the rest (10 of 43 row sets, 16 rows). Each prints at the precision its own draw count determines---both endpoints four Monte-Carlo standard errors clear of the nearest rounding boundary, over $200$ seeds and verified on the run that bought it. Two carry two decimals (the glycol ethers, at $1.2\times10^{8}$ draws), 9 carry one, and 11 carry two with a superscript giving their endpoints' Monte-Carlo standard deviation in units of that last digit. A further 2 (aldehyde; halogenated $\vert$ water as solute) no seed moves at all, their two-way resample having about 10 distinct compositions: a bootstrap with nothing left to resample, not a converged one. The per-cell verdict, its draw count and its cost at either precision are on the deposited record (\S\ref{sec:si-map}).
